standard_prerequisites.name: Basic Galois theory: invariants of a finite Galois extension and the orbit polynomial
standard_prerequisites.reference: Standard Galois theory of a finite stage: for a finite Galois extension k'/k with group G, the G-invariant elements of the base change of A to k' are exactly the elements of A (proof lines 921-925)
standard_prerequisites.use: Used to see that the coefficients of P(T) = prod_{sigma in G}(T - sigma(x)) lie in A; the construction of the polynomial, the passage to a finite stage and the radical argument are all retained.

standard_prerequisites.name: Radical ideals and the correspondence between closed subsets and radical ideals
standard_prerequisites.reference: Standard commutative algebra, used at proof lines 914-915 and 930-932
standard_prerequisites.use: The closed subset T-bar is encoded by its radical ideal I-bar inside the base change of A to k-bar; the proof shows that I-bar equals the radical of the ideal generated by I in that base change, and reads off T = V(I).

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case X = Spec(A) and let I-bar in A ⊗_k k-bar be the radical ideal of T-bar, so that the Galois invariance of T-bar becomes sigma(I-bar) = I-bar for every sigma in Gal(k-bar/k) (proof lines 913-917).

For an arbitrary x in I-bar, find a finite Galois extension k'/k contained in k-bar with x in A ⊗_k k', set G = Gal(k'/k) and form the orbit polynomial P(T) = prod_{sigma in G}(T - sigma(x)) in (A ⊗_k k')[T]; conclude that P is monic with coefficients in (A ⊗_k k')^G = A, hence that its coefficients a_i lie in I := A cap I-bar (proof lines 918-927).

Deduce from P(x) = 0 and a_i in I that x^d = -a_1 x^{d-1} - ... - a_d lies in I(A ⊗_k k-bar), so that every x in I-bar lies in the radical of I(A ⊗_k k-bar); conclude I-bar = rad(I(A ⊗_k k-bar)) and that T = V(I) is the required closed subset with inverse image T-bar (proof lines 928-932).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to X = Spec(A) affine; the closed subset T-bar corresponds to a radical ideal I-bar of A ⊗_k k-bar, and Galois invariance of T-bar translates into sigma(I-bar) = I-bar for all sigma in Gal(k-bar/k) (proof lines 913-917).
Finiteness reduction: for x in I-bar there is a finite Galois extension k'/k inside k-bar with x in A ⊗_k k'; put G = Gal(k'/k) (proof lines 918-920).

Orbit polynomial: P(T) = prod_{sigma in G}(T - sigma(x)) is monic and, by basic Galois theory, has coefficients in (A ⊗_k k')^G = A; writing P(T) = T^d + a_1 T^{d-1} + ... + a_d, each a_i lies in A cap I-bar = I because sigma(I-bar) = I-bar (proof lines 921-927).
Radical step: P(x) = 0 gives x^d = -a_1 x^{d-1} - ... - a_d in I(A ⊗_k k-bar), so every element of I-bar lies in the radical of I(A ⊗_k k-bar) (proof lines 928-930).
Conclusion: I-bar is the radical of I(A ⊗_k k-bar), so the closed subset T = V(I) of X has inverse image T-bar in X_k-bar (proof lines 931-932).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a possibly infinite Galois extension k-bar/k, a k-scheme X and a closed subset T-bar of X_k-bar that is stable under every sigma in Gal(k-bar/k), and asks for a closed subset T of X whose inverse image is T-bar (statement lines 900-909). After the reduction to X = Spec(A) the proof has to descend a radical ideal I-bar of the infinite tensor product A ⊗_k k-bar along the Galois action, and the two steps that are not formal are the finiteness reduction - an arbitrary x in I-bar already lies in A ⊗_k k' for some finite Galois subextension k'/k, so that the orbit polynomial P(T) = prod_{sigma in G}(T - sigma(x)) can be formed and is monic of degree |G| (proof lines 918-923) - and the identification of the invariants of that finite stage with A, which puts all coefficients a_i into A and hence, by sigma-invariance of I-bar, into I = A cap I-bar (proof lines 924-927). Only then does P(x) = 0 yield x^d in I(A ⊗_k k-bar), i.e. membership in a radical, which is what turns Galois invariance into an actual descent statement for closed subsets (proof lines 928-931).
